title: Lightweight Seat Track Interface Fittings for High-Density Economy Layouts
abstract: Proposal for a titanium seat track interface fitting that halves the fitting mass in nine-abreast economy layouts, aimed at operators whose cabin weight has grown past the point where the layout still pays.

sections.reason: Operators moving to nine-abreast economy have found the cabin mass growing faster than the seat count: the interface fittings that spread the seat leg load into the track were sized for a six-abreast pitch and are simply duplicated as the pitch tightens. On a 300-seat layout that is 1 200 fittings, and at the current mass it costs 340 kilogrammes against the six-abreast baseline. Two operators have asked whether a lighter fitting exists. There is no in-service problem driving this; it is a weight and therefore a fuel burn proposal, and it is presented as such.
sections.description: The steel interface fitting is replaced by a machined titanium item of the same footprint but with a hollowed web and a re-profiled shear lug. The forward seat light assembly HA869323-98 and the forward decor panel assembly KE7135-87 are unaffected but are disturbed during the change and are listed for handling. The forward seat track intercostal D5350121789008 is retained; only the fitting that clamps to it changes. Cushioned loop clamps EN220364-30 that carry the seat power harness along the track are replaced by a narrower item so that the harness still clears the new lug profile. The lower seat curtain rail position 7599DQ and the upper seat track lock actuator position 8300VU are both re-shimmed. Work is in the cabin with the seats removed, zones 243, 244 and 253. Detail is on drawings D53501271572 and D53501228696.
sections.effects: Estimated mass reduction of 168 kilogrammes on a 300-seat layout, distributed along the cabin, with no reportable balance effect. No electrical load change. The titanium fitting is interchangeable with the steel item at seat level, which is deliberate: an operator can change fittings a zone at a time during a cabin refresh rather than in one event. Seat certification is unaffected because the load path and the footprint do not change. The cabin layout drawing set and the seat installation task require update. The proposal has not yet been costed against the titanium machining rate, which is the main open commercial question.
sections.embodiment_note: Proposal only. If launched, embodiment would be during a scheduled cabin refresh when the seats are out anyway, adding an estimated one and a half days. No production cut-in is proposed because the fitting standard is tied to the seat supplier catalogue rather than to the aircraft build standard.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must establish whether the narrower harness clamp is compatible with the seat power standard already installed, whether the titanium fitting can be qualified against the existing sixteen-g dynamic seat test evidence without a new test, and what the machining cost does to the payback period.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin; no reportable shift
type_data.production_impact: No cut-in proposed; the fitting sits in the seat supplier catalogue
